import: import type { NavItem, NavEntity, NavAccordion, NavSection, NavBadge } from '@faclon-labs/iosense-shell'
purpose: The rail's data model. This package ships the rail's BEHAVIOUR — hover peek, the tooltip that only fires on an unreadable label, the accordion that opens itself on a deep link, the flyout in the 48px strip, the badge that becomes a dot when collapsed. None of it depends on which rows are in the rail, so the rows are data the host supplies and the rail renders NOTHING by default.

useInstead.when: You want a nav to start from.
useInstead.use: Copy demo/placeholderNav.tsx. It is six rows that exist only to demonstrate the three shapes — two entities with the two badge kinds, one accordion, one section — and it is NOT exported. The product rows it replaced were our pages.

useInstead.when: You want the iosense product itself.
useInstead.use: npm run dev. The demo is the product configuration; the package deliberately ships none of it.

decision: A plain destination? -> NavEntity: { id, label, icon }.
A destination with sub-pages under it? -> NavAccordion: add `children`. The parent becomes a disclosure control and is NOT navigable.
A visual grouping of sibling destinations, with a heading? -> NavSection: { kind: 'section', id, label, items }. It is NOT an ancestor and never appears in a breadcrumb.
An annotation on a row? -> `badge`. A number -> kind 'count'. A word -> kind 'word'.

defaults.items: [] — an empty rail. That is the export: the chrome, not our content.
defaults.tone: 'info' for a plain quantity (Neutral). 'alert' only when the number ITSELF is the bad news (Negative + Intense). 'label' for a word like Beta (Notice, and no collapsed dot).
defaults.defaultOpenGroups: Every section id, no accordion. A folded section in a fresh install is a hairline with no affordance to unfold it and it strands every row inside; a folded accordion still shows its parent row.
defaults.icon size: NAV_ICON_SIZE (14). The SDK's icon slot stays 16px; 14 is the drawn size inside it. Mixing 14 and 16 in one rail makes the icon column look ragged.

propRules.rule: ids must be unique across the WHOLE tree, including accordion children and section items.
propRules.why: activeId is matched against them, and React keys off them. Two rows with one id means both light up as active.

propRules.rule: An accordion's parent id is not a page.
propRules.why: It has no content of its own — landing on it shows an empty page. Map it to a real child and run every incoming id through resolveSection().

propRules.rule: Write the section-default map out; never use children[0].
propRules.why: In the iosense nav, Workflows' first child is a specific RECORD — 'Create company when a deal closes' — which is a nonsense landing page. Reports' first child happens to be right, which is exactly what would make an implicit first-child rule look correct until Workflows proved it wrong.

propRules.rule: badge is a Counter or a Badge, never a Chip.
propRules.why: Chip renders a <button> and the nav row is already a <button>. Nesting them is invalid HTML.

propRules.rule: A count goes in `kind: 'count'`, a word in `kind: 'word'`. Never a number as a string.
propRules.why: The axis is the answer type, not the look. The union is explicit rather than sniffed from the string precisely so "12" cannot silently take the Badge branch.

propRules.rule: Counts are capped at 99 by the rail.
propRules.why: Counter has NO default max — an uncapped count renders in full and stretches the row it sits in.

propRules.rule: isRecord only means something inside an accordion.
propRules.why: It marks a row as one INSTANCE rather than a page, which draws its tree branch differently. On a top-level row it does nothing.

propRules.rule: Sections do not nest, and accordions do not nest inside accordions.
propRules.why: The rail is two levels deep by design. A third level has nowhere to go in the 48px strip, where the flyout is already the escape hatch for level two.

propRules.rule: Pass the SAME array to AppSideNav/IosenseShell and to buildTrail.
propRules.why: buildTrail derives the hierarchy from it. Two different arrays is how a trail starts claiming a page sits somewhere the rail does not put it.

Correct data should be easy to write. The CSS clamp is a safety net for data that is wrong, not a licence to ignore the constant — a rail whose source says size={32} everywhere is a rail nobody can reason about.

propRules.rule: label is a string. It is not a ReactNode, and that is on purpose.
propRules.why: Arbitrary markup cannot be measured for truncation, so the tooltip rule — show the label only when it is clipped — would silently stop working. The type IS the rule.

propRules.rule: Do not restyle a nav row from outside.
propRules.why: The glyph size, the label type scale, the single line and the row height are the shape of the rail. A host stylesheet that changes one of them changes it for one product and not the next, which is the inconsistency the package exists to prevent.
propRules.instead: If a row needs to say something extra, that is what the badge slot is for.

propRules.rule: badge is a union, not a node.
propRules.why: The collapsed dot is DERIVED from it — kind and tone decide whether a dot is drawn and what colour. A node could not be inspected for that, so the 48px strip would lose the signal entirely.

composition.renders: Consumed by AppSideNav (and AppNavDrawer, which gets the same array — one nav, two presentations) and read by buildTrail.
composition.provides: navPageIds(items) for every navigable id, navParents(items) for the page-to-accordion map, and isSection / isAccordion as the type guards.

antiPatterns.pattern: Looking for a sample nav to import.
antiPatterns.why: Those are our pages — Zomato, Steam Trap, Memory B. A client installing this package and getting them is the exact failure the data model exists to prevent.
antiPatterns.instead: Copy it into your own file and replace every row.

antiPatterns.why: design-sdk's header falls through to its own built-in iosense mark, so the install silently ships our identity next to their nav.
antiPatterns.instead: Pass your own node. It stays put in the 48px header, collapsed and expanded.

antiPatterns.pattern: Putting a section in the breadcrumb trail.
antiPatterns.why: A section groups rows visually; it is not an ancestor. Devices sits under Connect in the rail and its trail is just 'Devices' — you cannot navigate to Connect.
antiPatterns.instead: Let buildTrail decide. It only walks accordions.

antiPatterns.pattern: Giving the accordion crumb an id so it is clickable.
antiPatterns.why: It is not a page. Pointing it at the accordion's first child makes a crumb whose job is to go UP move the reader SIDEWAYS into a sibling instead.
antiPatterns.instead: Leave it id-less. AppTopBar draws it as inert text.

antiPatterns.pattern: Reaching for tone 'alert' for any count you want noticed.
antiPatterns.why: It only works as a signal while nothing else borrows it. Twelve accounts and three deals are not news, they are furniture — and red on a sales pipeline reads as '3 problems'.
antiPatterns.instead: 'info'. Reach for 'alert' only when the number itself is the bad news.

antiPatterns.pattern: Importing a sample nav from the package.
antiPatterns.why: There is none, and there will not be. A shell has no opinion about what a product pages are. The demo has a six-row placeholder in demo/placeholderNav.tsx that exists only to make the accordion, the section and the collapse clickable.
antiPatterns.instead: Write your own NavItem[]. Copy demo/placeholderNav.tsx for the shapes if it helps.

antiPatterns.pattern: Passing a differently-sized icon because a row needs emphasis.
antiPatterns.why: It will be clamped to 14px, so the emphasis will not appear and the intent is lost in the source. Emphasis in a rail comes from the badge and the active state, not from icon size.
antiPatterns.instead: A badge with tone alert, or nothing.

antiPatterns.pattern: Wrapping a label to fit a long name.
antiPatterns.why: It cannot wrap — nowrap is enforced — and if it could, the row height would change and the icon column would look broken.
antiPatterns.instead: Let it ellipsise. The tooltip shows the full text, and that is the only case an expanded row shows one.

sizing.icon: 14px square, ENFORCED. The icon slot > svg is sized in CSS, and icon libraries set width/height as presentation attributes which CSS beats without !important — so a stray size={64} in nav data is clamped rather than catastrophic. Measured: rows fed size 8, 32 and 64 all render 14x14, all row heights stay 32, and every label still starts at x=40.
sizing.iconSlot: 16px, the SDK own. Untouched, so every label starts at the same x whatever the glyph does. That is why the glyph is 14 and not 16 — icons read lighter without moving the icon column.
sizing.label: One line, white-space: nowrap with text-overflow: ellipsis. A wrapped label changes the row height, and rows of differing heights make the icon column look broken. The clipped case is exactly what the tooltip exists for.
sizing.fontSize: 14px / weight 400 / --line-height-200 for a nav row; 12px for a section label, one step down so the hierarchy reads. The ACTIVE row keeps weight 400 — the SDK bolds it and that is overridden, because the row is already marked by background and ink and bolding reflows the text as you navigate.
sizing.rowHeight: 32px, and it is a consequence of the above rather than a separate rule. Nothing a host passes may change it.

variants.expanded: The 240px panel. Header shows logo + org name; a row is [icon] Label [trailing slot]; a section shows its label and can be folded; an accordion unfolds IN PLACE below its parent. Tooltips appear only when a label is clipped.
variants.collapsed: The 48px strip. The LOGO DOES NOT MOVE — it is the rail fixed point. Labels and the trailing slot are hidden; a 6px dot on the icon replaces a count or an alert but NOT a word, because a label like Beta is not state worth surfacing in 48px. An accordion opens a FLYOUT beside the strip instead of unfolding. A section is FORCED OPEN — folded it would be a hairline with no affordance to unfold it, stranding every row inside. Every row gets a tooltip, and it quotes the badge the dot stands in for.
variants.peeked: THE THIRD STATE, and the one most often missed. Hovering the collapsed rail draws the panel at 240px as an OVERLAY over a 48px footprint, so nothing to its right moves. Open after 150ms, close after 100ms. Only PINNING sets data-sidenav-pinned and reflows the page. Never key behaviour on isPinned meaning open: during a peek the rail is expanded and not pinned, and anything that assumes otherwise is wrong for the whole hover.
variants.rowStates: default transparent + secondary ink; hover --background-gray-hover-light; pressed --background-gray-default; active --background-gray-default + primary ink (the ICON takes primary ink too); active+hover --background-gray-hover-dark so an active row still answers the pointer. The active row keeps font-weight 400 — the SDK bolds it and that is overridden, because the row is already marked by background and ink and bolding reflows the label as you navigate. Transitions are background-color and color at --fds-duration-quick and width at --fds-duration-moderate, never all. All of this is the package: a host supplies no colours.
